Class SwerveDrive

java.lang.Object
yams.core.mechanisms.swerve.SwerveDrive
Direct Known Subclasses:
SwerveDrive, SwerveDrive
public class SwerveDrive extends Object
Swerve Drive mechanism.

This core class holds swerve state, odometry, and physics simulation only. Command factories such as drive() live on SwerveDrive, which extends this class. See that class's Javadoc for a full usage example.

  • Constructor Details

    • SwerveDrive

      protected SwerveDrive(SwerveDriveConfig<?> config)
      Create a SwerveDrive.
      Parameters:
      config - SwerveDriveConfig for the drive.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - on a real robot (not in simulation), if no gyro supplier was set with SwerveDriveConfig.withGyro(java.util.function.Supplier).
      SmartMotorControllerConfigurationException - if a module's drive motor has no mechanism circumference configured (e.g. via SwerveModuleConfig.withWheelRadius(Distance)), so its position cannot be converted to a distance.
      Implementation Note:
      Protected so only SwerveDrive can construct this.

  • Method Details

    • startDriveToPoseTuning

      public void startDriveToPoseTuning()
      Reset the auto-align PID controllers and pull the live-tuned values (from NetworkTables) into this SwerveDrive. Intended to be wired into a periodic/scheduled callback by the command layer, e.g. via yams.commands2.swerve.SwerveDrive's drive-to-pose tuning command.

    • applyTuningValues

      public void applyTuningValues()
      Apply the live-tuned values (from NetworkTables) to this SwerveDrive's drive-to-pose controllers. Intended to be wired into a periodic/scheduled callback by the command layer.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the auto-align tuning toggle is enabled and a gyro angular velocity scale factor is configured with SwerveDriveConfig.withGyroAngularVelocityScaleFactor(double) but no gyro supplier was set with SwerveDriveConfig.withGyro(java.util.function.Supplier).

      Returns:
      The robot's attitude.

    • getSimPose

      public org.wpilib.math.geometry.Pose2d getSimPose()
      Get the simulated pose of the robot, assuming the SwerveModuleVelocitys commanded to the modules are met perfectly. Useful for feeding a simulated vision system with ground-truth poses under perfect-world conditions.
      Returns:
      Simulated Pose2d of the robot. Only updated in simulation by simIterate(); on a real robot this remains the configured starting pose.

      Set the SwerveModuleVelocitys of the swerve drive directly.

    • setSwerveModuleStates

      public void setSwerveModuleStates(org.wpilib.math.kinematics.SwerveModuleVelocity[] states, org.wpilib.units.measure.Force[] feedforwardForces)
      Set the SwerveModuleVelocitys of the swerve drive directly, with an additional drive wheel feedforward Force applied per module, e.g. from a PathPlanner set-point generator.
      Parameters:
      states - SwerveModuleVelocitys to use, must be the same count as the swerve drive is configured order is Clockwise from FL.
      feedforwardForces - Feedforward Forces to apply, one per module in the same FL, FR, BL, BR order as states.
      Implementation Note:
      Not compatible with AdvantageKit if MapleSim is defined.

    • getStateFromRobotRelativeChassisSpeeds

      public org.wpilib.math.kinematics.SwerveModuleVelocity[] getStateFromRobotRelativeChassisSpeeds(org.wpilib.math.kinematics.ChassisVelocities robotRelativeChassisSpeeds)
      Get the SwerveModuleVelocitys of the swerve drive given a robot relative chassis speed. When a maximum module speed is configured with SwerveDriveConfig.withMaximumModuleSpeed(LinearVelocity), the module speeds are scaled down together so none exceeds it, also respecting SwerveDriveConfig.withMaximumChassisSpeed(LinearVelocity, AngularVelocity) if set, which keeps the direction of travel and rotation intact.
      Parameters:
      robotRelativeChassisSpeeds - Robot relative ChassisVelocities.
      Returns:
      SwerveModuleVelocitys of the swerve drive.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if a gyro angular velocity scale factor is configured with SwerveDriveConfig.withGyroAngularVelocityScaleFactor(double) but no gyro supplier was set with SwerveDriveConfig.withGyro(java.util.function.Supplier).

    • getRobotRelativeChassisSpeedsFromState

    • setRobotRelativeChassisSpeeds

      public void setRobotRelativeChassisSpeeds(org.wpilib.math.kinematics.ChassisVelocities robotRelativeChassisSpeeds, org.wpilib.units.measure.Force[] feedforwardForces)
      Set robot relative chassis speeds, with an additional drive wheel feedforward Force applied per module, e.g. from a PathPlanner set-point generator.
      Parameters:
      robotRelativeChassisSpeeds - Robot relative chassis speeds.
      feedforwardForces - Feedforward Forces to apply, one per module in FL, FR, BL, BR order. Pass an empty array to apply no feedforward.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if feedforwardForces is not empty and its length does not match the number of modules.
      IllegalStateException - if a gyro angular velocity scale factor is configured with SwerveDriveConfig.withGyroAngularVelocityScaleFactor(double) but no gyro supplier was set with SwerveDriveConfig.withGyro(java.util.function.Supplier).

    • resetOdometry

      public void resetOdometry(org.wpilib.math.geometry.Pose2d pose)
      Resets odometry to the given pose, and sets the gyro to read the pose's heading. Field relative driving and heading control use the gyro, so keeping it aligned with the pose makes them agree with the reset pose. Module positions do not need to be reset when calling this method.
      Parameters:
      pose - The pose to set the odometry to. Field relative, blue-origin where 0deg is facing towards RED alliance.

    • driveToPoseSetpoint

      public org.wpilib.math.kinematics.ChassisVelocities driveToPoseSetpoint(org.wpilib.math.geometry.Pose2d targetPose)
      Drive to the target pose, primarily for use in Live Tuning, could also be used for setpoint commands.
      Parameters:
      targetPose - Pose to drive towards.
      Returns:
      robot-relative ChassisVelocities to drive the robot to the given pose.
      Throws:
      SwerveDriveConfigurationException - if the translation PID controller is not configured.
      SwerveDriveConfigurationException - if the rotation PID controller is not configured.
      Implementation Note:
      Remember to call resetRotationPID() and resetTranslationPID() before calling this method in a loop.

    • driveToPoseSetpoint

      public org.wpilib.math.kinematics.ChassisVelocities driveToPoseSetpoint(org.wpilib.math.geometry.Pose2d targetPose, org.wpilib.math.geometry.Pose2d currentPose, org.wpilib.math.geometry.Rotation2d heading)
      Drive to the target pose from a given pose, e.g. a pose replayed from a log. The translation speed is the translation PID output toward the target, proportional to the distance for a P controller.
      Parameters:
      targetPose - Pose to drive towards.
      currentPose - Pose of the robot.
      heading - Heading of the robot, used to convert the result to robot-relative speeds.
      Returns:
      robot-relative ChassisVelocities to drive the robot to the given pose.
      Throws:
      SwerveDriveConfigurationException - if the translation PID controller is not configured.
      SwerveDriveConfigurationException - if the rotation PID controller is not configured.
      Implementation Note:
      Remember to call resetRotationPID() and resetTranslationPID() before calling this method in a loop.

    • addVisionMeasurement

      public void addVisionMeasurement(org.wpilib.math.geometry.Pose2d robotPose, double timestamp, org.wpilib.math.linalg.Matrix<org.wpilib.math.numbers.N3, org.wpilib.math.numbers.N1> visionMeasurementStdDevs)
      Add a vision measurement to the SwerveDrivePoseEstimator and update the gyro reading with the given timestamp of the vision measurement.
      Parameters:
      robotPose - Robot Pose2d as measured by vision.
      timestamp - Timestamp the measurement was taken as time since startup, should be taken from Timer.getTimestamp() or similar sources.
      visionMeasurementStdDevs - Vision measurement standard deviation that will be sent to the SwerveDrivePoseEstimator.The standard deviation of the vision measurement, for best accuracy calculate the standard deviation at 2 or more points and fit a line to it with the calculated optimal standard deviation. (Units should be meters per pixel). By optimizing this you can get * vision accurate to inches instead of feet.

    • setVisionMeasurementStdDevs

      public void setVisionMeasurementStdDevs(org.wpilib.math.linalg.Matrix<org.wpilib.math.numbers.N3, org.wpilib.math.numbers.N1> visionMeasurementStdDevs)
      Sets the pose estimator's trust of global measurements. This might be used to change trust in vision measurements after the autonomous period, or to change trust as distance to a vision target increases.
      Parameters:
      visionMeasurementStdDevs - Standard deviations of the vision measurements. Increase these numbers to trust global measurements from vision less. This matrix is in the form [x, y, theta], with units in meters and radians.

    • getDesiredChassisSpeeds

      public org.wpilib.math.kinematics.ChassisVelocities getDesiredChassisSpeeds()
      Get the last-commanded desired robot-relative ChassisVelocities of the drive. This is the value cached by setRobotRelativeChassisSpeeds(ChassisVelocities) (which setFieldRelativeChassisSpeeds(ChassisVelocities) and SwerveDrive.drive(java.util.function.Supplier) funnel through) and published on every updateTelemetry() call.
      Returns:
      Robot-relative ChassisVelocities last commanded to the drive. Defaults to a zeroed ChassisVelocities if the drive has never been commanded.
      Implementation Note:
      It is a setpoint, not a measurement of actual robot motion. Use getRobotRelativeSpeed() or getFieldRelativeSpeed() instead if you need the drive's actual measured speed.
